topicName: Indexing Strategies (B-Tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, Hash)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering PostgreSQL Indexing Strategies: B-Tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, and Hash"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right index in PostgreSQL is critical for maintaining high query performance as your dataset scales. PostgreSQL offers multiple index access methods, each designed for specific data types and query patterns. This tutorial explores B-Tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, and Hash indexes, explaining when and how to use them effectively."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. B-Tree Indexes (The Default)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"B-Tree is the default index type in PostgreSQL. It is a self-balancing tree that excels at equality and range queries on data that can be sorted. You can use B-Tree for data types like numbers, text, dates, and timestamps."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supported operators: <, <=, =, >=, >, BETWEEN, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. GIN (Generalized Inverted Index)"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"GIN indexes are designed for data values that contain multiple component elements, such as arrays, JSONB documents, and full-text search vectors. Instead of indexing the entire column value, GIN indexes individual elements (like keys in JSON or words in text), pointing back to the rows containing them."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Best for: JSONB containment queries, array overlaps, and tsvector full-text search."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"CREATE INDEX idx_documents_data ON documents USING GIN (data);"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. GiST (Generalized Search Tree)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"GiST is a balanced tree structure infrastructure that allows the development of custom access methods. It is heavily used for geometric data (PostGIS), ranges, and nearest-neighbor searches. GiST is lossy for some types, meaning it may return candidate rows that must then be rechecked."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Best for: Geometric data types (Polygon, Point), range types, and full-text search."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"CREATE INDEX idx_locations_coordinates ON locations USING GiST (coordinates);"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. BRIN (Block Range Index)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"BRIN is designed for massive tables with naturally ordered data, such as timestamp logs or sequential IDs. Instead of indexing every single row, BRIN stores summary statistics (minimum and maximum values) for blocks of physical disk pages. This results in a drastically smaller index size compared to B-Tree."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Best for: Append-only time-series data and massive tables where rows are naturally sorted on disk."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"CREATE INDEX idx_sensor_logs_created_at ON sensor_logs USING BRIN (created_at);"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Hash Indexes"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Hash indexes store a 32-bit hash of the index value. Because they only support simple equality checks, they are an alternative to B-Tree when dealing with long strings or large keys where only exact matches are queried. PostgreSQL hash indexes are now WAL-logged and crash-safe."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supported operators: = (Equality only)."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_token ON user_sessions USING HASH (session_token);"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary & Best Practices"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always analyze your query workload using EXPLAIN ANALYZE before deploying indexes to production. While indexes speed up reads, they impose a write overhead during INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations. Choose B-Tree for general use, GIN for JSONB/Arrays, GiST for Geometry, BRIN for massive ordered logs, and Hash for strict equality lookups on large keys."}]
